title: Frontiers: The Interplay of User-Generated Content, Content Industry Revenues, and Platform Regulation: Quasi-Experimental Evidence from YouTube
authors: Nils Wlomert; Dominik Papies; Michel Clement; Martin Spann
eligible_reason: Single common onset: step_dummy switches on for treated tracks (previously blocked on YouTube in Germany) at the November 2016 GEMA-YouTube agreement; matching week 2016-10-31. One adoption cohort, so not staggered. Main estimates also use inverse-propensity weights (WeightIt, method ps), which the protocol excludes as analysis weights.
design_notes: code/analysis_main.R: feols(log outcome ~ step_dummy | isrc + week, weights = IPTW) for premium streams, ad-funded streams, downloads; full model interacts step_dummy with six track characteristics. robust_noweight.R: same without IPTW (with interactions). weekly_effects.R: weekly effects (Figure 4). placebo_test_pretreat.R, robust_pretreat_trend.R: Tables E1-E2. matching*.R: propensity weights at 2016-10-31.
data_files_note: code/readme.txt: due to an NDA the data are not the real data; variables 'are derived from the original variables such that the correlation structure between the variables is largely preserved'; 25% random sample of tracks; outcomes named *_synth.
screener_notes: Screened from package only. The on-disk extraction only contains an empty code/ directory; I unzipped the code/ folder from _archive_mksc.2022.0080.zip into the scratchpad to read it (regression inventory was empty for this reason). Not staggered; data disguised.
